root_cause_history: PR #268 added the aria-label inside vc-breadcrumbs-item.vue. The button axe flags is the breadcrumbs overflow trigger that vc-blade.vue supplies via the #trigger slot, and a slot override REPLACES the labelled button VcBreadcrumbs provides. QA's 08-04 re-test diagnosed this; PR #282 moved the fix onto the blade's own trigger and raised its target size 22x36 -> 24x36.

notes: STRUCTURAL FINDING: the breadcrumb trail collapses ENTIRELY on every item blade — nav[aria-label=Breadcrumb] > ol contains exactly ONE <li>, the overflow dropdown, and Maximize does not expand it (so the collapse is unconditional, not width-driven). Three consequences: it explains why the original violation hit every item blade; the inline vc-breadcrumbs-item path that PR #268 fixed is effectively NEVER exercised in this app (so #268 was not merely aimed at the wrong component — its target does not render here at all); and it constrains AC3, because titled crumbs could only be evidenced inside the expanded overflow menu (aria-label and title both null there, so the name comes from the crumb's own text — they did NOT acquire a generic label), while an inline-rendered titled crumb could not be tested because this build never produces one.

The German leg is BLOCKED — an environment limit, not a defect. Confirmed independently through the real UI: user menu > Language renders exactly one option, English, marked active; a DOM sweep for English/Deutsch/German/Français/Español/Русский/de-DE found only English. The framework ships 'Weitere Brotkrümel anzeigen' (proven in the bundle) but the selectable-locale list is registered by the APP, not the framework. No locale was forced via storage or app state. Same limitation independently hit on VCST-5668 today — if no deployed environment offers a second locale, every 'en + de' AC in this product is unverifiable at runtime.
